chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ibn Ri'ab, from Durays al-Kunasi, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:

"No remission is granted regarding the hudud that belong to Allah, apart from the Imam. But as for what belongs to the rights of people within a hadd, there is no harm in its being remitted apart from the Imam."

key_terms.حُقُوقِ ٱلنَّاسِ: the rights of people, meaning private human claims
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or objection
key_terms.لِلَّهِ: belonging to Allah, meaning divine right rather than private claim
key_terms.ٱلْإِمَامِ: the Imam, the legitimate authority over enforcement and remission in such matters
key_terms.ٱلْحُدُودِ: the prescribed legal punishments or fixed penal limits

ai.seo_question: Can hadd punishments be waived without the Imam in cases involving the rights of Allah or the rights of people?
ai.summary: This hadith distinguishes between hudud connected to the rights of Allah and matters within a hadd related to the rights of people. It states that remission of Allah's hudud is not permitted independently of the Imam, while a person's own right within such a case may be waived without the Imam.
